name: Unthread: Meditations on Discontinuous Memory
creator: Callum Ndiaye-Bergström
description: A hybrid memoir-philosophy text by a former BCI technician who suffered a catastrophic neural feed corruption at age 34, losing approximately eleven years of accessible autobiographical memory. Ndiaye-Bergström writes about reconstructing a self from external records — friends' accounts, archived feed logs, physical photographs — and what it means to be a person whose continuity is a collaborative fiction. The prose is lucid and strangely calm, which many readers find more unsettling than anguish would be.
medium: neural feed text (primary); physical paperback (second printing by independent press)
cultural_impact: Became essential reading in BCI ethics circles and is now assigned in several Tier 3 technical academies, unusual for a work that is fundamentally personal rather than instructional; it articulated an experience that millions of people with BCI damage had never seen named.
controversy: The corponation responsible for the faulty BCI firmware that caused Ndiaye-Bergström's corruption — never named in the text, referred to only as 'the manufacturer' — is widely believed to be Halvex-subsidiary NeuralCore. NeuralCore has issued no comment but quietly settled with Ndiaye-Bergström under undisclosed terms prior to publication.
story_hooks: Ndiaye-Bergström's recovered feed logs contain a gap within the gap — a period even the external records can't account for — and someone has been paying to keep that specific window inaccessible.

A support community that formed around the book has been infiltrated by NeuralCore representatives gathering data on the long-term effects of the firmware flaw, and the community's moderator has just figured it out.

The physical second printing contains a handwritten note in some copies — the same note, reproduced in facsimile — that was never in the neural version and that changes the meaning of the final chapter entirely.
